# Animation tools

Skeletal animation, controllers, IK, bone attachments and cinematic sequences.

12 tools in the `animation` category. Badges: **read-only** tools never change the project; **mutating** tools are undoable and attributed; **open-world** tools reach outside the engine and MCP clients ask before running them.

| Tool | Summary |
|---|---|
| [`animation_list`](#animation_list) | Skeleton and clips of a rigged model or animated character. |
| [`animator_setup`](#animator_setup) | Create a state machine controller (*.animctl.json) for a character and assign it. |
| [`animation_preview`](#animation_preview) | Render a character posed at a clip or state at given times (editor preview; the scene is not changed). |
| [`animator_set`](#animator_set) | Set an animator's parameters and triggers, or play a state/clip with a crossfade — live while the simulation runs (same as Wander set_param / trigger / play_animation), or as the editor preview while editing. |
| [`bone_attach`](#bone_attach) | Make an entity follow a bone of an animated character: a sword in the right hand, a hat on the head, a lantern on the hip. |
| [`bone_ik`](#bone_ik) | Make a character's hand or foot reach a point with two-bone IK (the elbow/knee and shoulder/hip bend; bone lengths are kept): a hand on a door handle, rail or lever, a foot planted on a step. |
| [`sequence_create`](#sequence_create) | Create a cinematic sequence asset (*.sequence.json) and an entity whose `sequencer` plays it when the simulation starts. |
| [`sequence_key`](#sequence_key) | Add or replace keys in a sequence, many at once. |
| [`sequence_camera_shot`](#sequence_camera_shot) | Add a procedural camera move to a sequence — the quickest way to direct cinematics. |
| [`sequence_get`](#sequence_get) | A sequence's tracks (type, entity, property, key count and time span) and length; with `time`, the evaluated property values and live camera at that moment. |
| [`sequence_play`](#sequence_play) | Play or stop a sequence. |
| [`sequence_scrub`](#sequence_scrub) | Look at a sequence at any time without playing: renders through the sequence's live camera (cuts and shots) with every keyed property and animation applied, then restores the scene. |

### `animation_list` { #animation_list }

**List animations** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--ro" title="Never changes the scene">read-only</span>

Skeleton and clips of a rigged model or animated character. With `entity`: its animator's library (clips with duration and rootSpeed in m/s for locomotion clips), controller (parameters, states), current state, recent animation events and warnings. With `model`: a .anim library or an imported .glb/.gltf. With neither: every animation library in the project. bones=true lists bone names (for bone_attach, layer masks, look-at). Example: {"entity": "Hero"}.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `entity` | integer \| string |  | Character with an animator (or a child of one) |  |
| `model` | string |  | Animation library (.anim) or rigged model (.glb/.gltf), project-relative |  |
| `bones` | boolean |  | Include the bone hierarchy (default: true for model, false for entity) |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    animation_list {"entity": "Hero"}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call animation_list '{"entity": "Hero"}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "animation_list",
        "arguments": {
          "entity": "Hero"
        }
      }
    }
    ```

### `animator_setup` { #animator_setup }

**Set up animator** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--mut" title="Changes the project; undoable and attributed">mutating</span>

Create a state machine controller (*.animctl.json) for a character and assign it. preset=locomotion (default) finds idle/walk/run/jump clips by name and builds: parameter `speed` (m/s) driving a 1D blend Idle -> Walk -> Run whose thresholds are the clips' real root speeds (feet don't slide when you set speed to the actual velocity), and if there is a jump clip a `jump` trigger with Jump -> back to locomotion. preset=clips: one state per clip, no transitions (drive with play_animation). Override clip choices with `clips` ({"idle": "Breathe", "run": "Sprint"}), or pass a full `controller` document (parameters, layers with states/blend/blend2d, transitions with "when" conditions like "speed > 0.1 and grounded", exit times, events, masks) — it is validated with did-you-mean errors. Then drive it from Wander: set_param(self, "speed", v), trigger(self, "jump"), play_animation(self, "Wave").

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `entity` | integer \| string | yes | The character |  |
| `preset` | string |  | Generated controller (default locomotion) | `locomotion` `clips` |
| `clips` | object |  | Clip choice overrides: idle, walk, run, jump |  |
| `controller` | object |  | A full controller document instead of a preset |  |
| `path` | string |  | Where to save the controller (default: next to the library, &lt;name&gt;.animctl.json) |  |
| `library` | string |  | Animation library (.anim) if the character has none yet |  |
| `root_motion` | boolean |  | Move the character by its clips' root motion (default: unchanged) |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    animator_setup {"entity": "Knight", "root_motion": false}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call animator_setup '{"entity": "Knight", "root_motion": false}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "animator_setup",
        "arguments": {
          "entity": "Knight",
          "root_motion": false
        }
      }
    }
    ```

### `animation_preview` { #animation_preview }

**Preview animation** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--ro" title="Never changes the scene">read-only</span>

Render a character posed at a clip or state at given times (editor preview; the scene is not changed). Frames the character automatically (three_quarter / front / side / back) unless eye/target are given. times=[0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75] returns a contact sheet of images — check walk cycles, attacks, hand poses, props attached to bones. While playing, captures the live pose instead. Example: {"entity": "Hero", "clip": "Run", "times": [0, 0.2, 0.4]}.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `entity` | integer \| string | yes | The character (or any entity under its animator) |  |
| `clip` | string |  | Clip or state to show (default: what the animator plays by default) |  |
| `time` | number |  | Seconds into the clip/state (default 0) |  |
| `times` | number[] |  | Several times -&gt; one image each (max 8), e.g. a walk cycle contact sheet |  |
| `params` | object |  | Controller parameters for the preview, e.g. {"speed": 2.5} |  |
| `view` | string |  | Automatic framing (default three_quarter) | `three_quarter` `front` `side` `back` |
| `eye` | number[3] |  | Custom camera position (instead of automatic framing) |  |
| `target` | number[3] |  | Custom look-at point (with eye) |  |
| `width` | integer |  | Image width (default 512) |  |
| `height` | integer |  | Image height (default 512) |  |
| `save_path` | string |  | Also write the (first) PNG to this project-relative path |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    animation_preview {"entity": "Hero", "clip": "Run", "times": [0, 0.2, 0.4]}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call animation_preview '{"entity": "Hero", "clip": "Run", "times": [0, 0.2, 0.4]}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "animation_preview",
        "arguments": {
          "entity": "Hero",
          "clip": "Run",
          "times": [
            0,
            0.2,
            0.4
          ]
        }
      }
    }
    ```

### `animator_set` { #animator_set }

**Drive animator** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--mut" title="Changes the project; undoable and attributed">mutating</span>

Set an animator's parameters and triggers, or play a state/clip with a crossfade — live while the simulation runs (same as Wander set_param / trigger / play_animation), or as the editor preview while editing. Also sets look_at (head/spine IK toward an entity; "" clears), the editor preview mode/time. Returns the animator state. Example: {"entity": "Hero", "params": {"speed": 3}, "trigger": "jump"}.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `entity` | integer \| string | yes | The character |  |
| `params` | object |  | Parameter values, e.g. {"speed": 2.5, "grounded": true} |  |
| `trigger` | any |  | Trigger name or list of names |  |
| `play` | string |  | State or clip to crossfade to (editing: shown as the preview) |  |
| `fade` | number |  | Crossfade seconds (default 0.2) |  |
| `loop` | boolean |  | Loop the played clip (default: the state's setting; clips play once and return) |  |
| `layer` | integer |  | Layer index for play (default 0) |  |
| `time` | number |  | Editor preview time in seconds |  |
| `preview` | string |  | Editor preview mode | `rest` `pose` `play` |
| `look_at` | string |  | Entity the head turns toward ("" = off) |  |
| `preview_time` | number |  | Editing: show the default state (or `play`) at this time without saving it (live scrubbing) |  |
| `clear_preview` | boolean |  | Remove a preview set by play / preview_time while editing |  |

### `bone_attach` { #bone_attach }

**Attach to bone** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--mut" title="Changes the project; undoable and attributed">mutating</span>

Make an entity follow a bone of an animated character: a sword in the right hand, a hat on the head, a lantern on the hip. Validates the bone (did-you-mean; animation_list bones=true lists them), adds the `attach` component and (by default) parents the entity under the character. offset/rotation are in the bone's space. Example: {"entity": "Sword", "to": "Hero", "bone": "RightHand", "offset": [0, 0.08, 0.02]}.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `entity` | integer \| string | yes | The prop to attach |  |
| `to` | integer \| string | yes | The character (entity with the animator) |  |
| `bone` | string | yes | Bone name, e.g. RightHand, Head, mixamorig:Spine2 |  |
| `offset` | number[3] |  | Position in bone space (m) |  |
| `rotation` | number[3] |  | Rotation in bone space (Euler degrees) |  |
| `follow_scale` | boolean |  | Inherit the bone's scale (default false) |  |
| `parent` | boolean |  | Parent the prop under the character (default true) |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    bone_attach {"entity": "Sword", "to": "Hero", "bone": "RightHand", "offset": [0, 0.08, 0.02]}
    ```

### `bone_ik` { #bone_ik }

**Reach with IK** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--mut" title="Changes the project; undoable and attributed">mutating</span>

Make a character's hand or foot reach a point with two-bone IK (the elbow/knee and shoulder/hip bend; bone lengths are kept): a hand on a door handle, rail or lever, a foot planted on a step. Either give `entity` (an existing object becomes the effector — the bone reaches it) or a `position` (a new effector entity is created under the character; default: where the bone is now). Move or keyframe the effector (sequence_key transform.position) to animate the reach; `weight` blends with the animation. pole = bend direction in the character's space ([0,0,-1] knees forward; elbows usually [0,0,1]). Example: {"character": "Hero", "bone": "RightHand", "entity": "Door Handle"}.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `character` | integer \| string | yes | The character (entity with the animator) |  |
| `bone` | string | yes | End bone: LeftHand, RightHand, LeftFoot, RightFoot... |  |
| `entity` | integer \| string |  | Existing entity to reach (it gets the ik component) |  |
| `position` | number[3] |  | World position for a new effector entity |  |
| `name` | string |  | Name of the new effector (default "&lt;bone&gt; IK") |  |
| `weight` | number |  | 0..1 (default 1) |  |
| `pole` | number[3] |  | Bend direction in the character's space (default: keep the animated bend) |  |
| `match_rotation` | boolean |  | Also orient the bone like the effector (default false) |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    bone_ik {"character": "Hero", "bone": "RightHand", "entity": "Door Handle"}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call bone_ik '{"character": "Hero", "bone": "RightHand", "entity": "Door Handle"}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "bone_ik",
        "arguments": {
          "character": "Hero",
          "bone": "RightHand",
          "entity": "Door Handle"
        }
      }
    }
    ```

### `sequence_create` { #sequence_create }

**Create sequence** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--mut" title="Changes the project; undoable and attributed">mutating</span>

Create a cinematic sequence asset (*.sequence.json) and an entity whose `sequencer` plays it when the simulation starts. Then add content with sequence_key (keyed properties, camera cuts, events, animations) and sequence_camera_shot (orbit / dolly / crane / track / pan / static / path / flyover moves), check frames with sequence_scrub and play with sequence_play. `tracks` may hold a full track list (see docs/ANIMATION.md). Example: {"path": "cinematics/intro.sequence.json", "duration": 10}.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | Project-relative path ending in .sequence.json |  |
| `name` | string |  | Display name (default: file name) |  |
| `duration` | number |  | Length in seconds (0 = until the last key) |  |
| `tracks` | object[] |  | Initial tracks (optional) |  |
| `entity` | string |  | Entity to play it: an existing one gets the sequencer, a new name creates it (default: a new entity named after the sequence) |  |
| `play_on_start` | boolean |  | Start with the simulation (default true) |  |
| `loop` | boolean |  | Loop (default false) |  |
| `overwrite` | boolean |  | Replace an existing file |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    sequence_create {"path": "cinematics/intro.sequence.json", "duration": 10}
    ```

=== "CLI"

### `sequence_key` { #sequence_key }

**Key sequence** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--mut" title="Changes the project; undoable and attributed">mutating</span>

Add or replace keys in a sequence, many at once. `keys`: property keys {entity, property, t, value, ease} animating any component field ("transform.position", "transform.rotation", "light.intensity", "light.color", "camera.fov", "mesh.color", "mesh.emissive", "particles.rate", or "environment.sunElevation" without entity). ease: linear (default), step, smooth, ease_in, ease_out, auto (smooth spline through neighbours — best for camera paths) or [x1,y1,x2,y2] cubic-bezier. `camera_cuts`: [{t, camera}] which camera is live. `events`: [{t, event, target?}] Wander events. `animations`: [{entity, t, play, fade?, loop?, params?}] drive animators. A key at an existing time replaces it; replace=true clears touched tracks first. Example: {"sequence": "cinematics/intro.sequence.json", "keys": [{"entity": "Sun", "property": "light.intensity", "t": 0, "value": 0}, {"entity": "Sun", "property": "light.intensity", "t": 3, "value": 4, "ease": "smooth"}]}.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence` | any | yes | Sequence path (.sequence.json) or an entity with a sequencer |  |
| `keys` | object[] |  | Property keys {entity, property, t, value, ease} |  |
| `camera_cuts` | object[] |  | Camera cuts {t, camera} |  |
| `events` | object[] |  | Events {t, event, target} |  |
| `animations` | object[] |  | Animation keys {entity, t, play, fade, loop, params} |  |
| `replace` | boolean |  | Clear every touched track before adding (default false: merge) |  |
| `remove` | object[] |  | Tracks to delete: {entity, property} or {type} |  |
| `duration` | number |  | Set the sequence length (seconds) |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    sequence_key {"sequence": "cinematics/intro.sequence.json", "keys": [{"entity": "Sun", "property": "light.intensity", "t": 0, "value": 0}, {"entity": "Sun", "property": "light.intensity", "t": 3, "value": 4, "ease": "smooth"}]}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call sequence_key '{"sequence": "cinematics/intro.sequence.json", "keys": [{"entity": "Sun", "property": "light.intensity", "t": 0, "value": 0}, {"entity": "Sun", "property": "light.intensity", "t": 3, "value": 4, "ease": "smooth"}]}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

### `sequence_camera_shot` { #sequence_camera_shot }

**Camera shot** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--mut" title="Changes the project; undoable and attributed">mutating</span>

Add a procedural camera move to a sequence — the quickest way to direct cinematics. Shots are evaluated live each tick, so they follow moving targets. Kinds: orbit (around target; radius, height, from/to degrees), dolly (distance [far, near] along angle, or from/to points), crane (height [low, high]), track (side-on, slides from/to meters while following the target), pan (fixed position, look from/to: entities, points or yaw degrees), static (position looking at target), path (Catmull-Rom through points, looking at target or along the path), flyover (straight aerial pass over the target from the angle side: distance = half the pass length, height). fov: number or [from, to] (zoom), roll in degrees, ease (default smooth). cut=true (default) also switches to this camera at start. Missing cameras are created. Example: {"sequence": "Intro", "camera": "Cam A", "shot": "orbit", "target": "Hero", "start": 0, "duration": 5, "radius": 5, "height": 1.8, "from": -30, "to": 60}.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence` | any | yes | Sequence path or entity with a sequencer |  |
| `camera` | string |  | Camera entity (created if missing; default "Shot Camera") |  |
| `shot` | string | yes | Kind of move | `orbit` `dolly` `crane` `track` `pan` `static` `path` `flyover` |
| `start` | number |  | Start time in seconds (default: after the camera's previous shot) |  |
| `duration` | number | yes | Seconds |  |
| `target` | any |  | Entity name or [x,y,z] the camera frames |  |
| `offset` | number[3] |  | Added to the target point (e.g. [0, 1.6, 0] for eye height) |  |
| `radius` | number |  | orbit radius (m) |  |
| `height` | any |  | Camera height above the target: number or [from, to] |  |
| `distance` | any |  | Distance from the target: number or [from, to] |  |
| `angle` | number |  | Direction from the target (yaw degrees, 0 = +Z) |  |
| `from` | any |  | Start: angle (orbit/pan), lateral meters (track), point (dolly/pan) |  |
| `to` | any |  | End: like from |  |
| `position` | number[3] |  | Camera position (pan, static) |  |
| `points` | array[] |  | Path points (path) |  |
| `pitch` | number |  | Pan pitch (degrees) |  |
| `fov` | any |  | Field of view: number or [from, to] (zoom) |  |
| `roll` | number |  | Dutch angle (degrees) |  |
| `ease` | any |  | linear, smooth (default), ease_in, ease_out or [x1,y1,x2,y2] |  |
| `cut` | boolean |  | Switch to this camera at start (default true) |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    sequence_camera_shot {"sequence": "Intro", "camera": "Cam A", "shot": "orbit", "target": "Hero", "start": 0, "duration": 5, "radius": 5, "height": 1.8, "from": -30, "to": 60}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call sequence_camera_shot '{"sequence": "Intro", "camera": "Cam A", "shot": "orbit", "target": "Hero", "start": 0, "duration": 5, "radius": 5, "height": 1.8, "from": -30, "to": 60}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",

        "name": "sequence_camera_shot",
    ```

### `sequence_play` { #sequence_play }

**Play sequence** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--mut" title="Changes the project; undoable and attributed">mutating</span>

Play or stop a sequence. Sequences run in the simulation: while editing this starts the simulation (like sim_control play) and plays the sequence from `from`; while playing it restarts / seeks or stops it. Sequencers with playOnStart start by themselves when the simulation starts. Watch with viewport_capture view="scene" after sim_control step.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence` | any | yes | Entity with a sequencer, or a sequence path played by one |  |
| `action` | string |  | Default play | `play` `stop` |
| `from` | number |  | Start time in seconds (default 0) |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    sequence_play {"sequence": "Director", "action": "play", "from": 0}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call sequence_play '{"sequence": "Director", "action": "play", "from": 0}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "sequence_play",
        "arguments": {
          "sequence": "Director",
          "action": "play",
          "from": 0
        }
      }
    }
    ```

### `sequence_scrub` { #sequence_scrub }

**Scrub sequence** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--mut" title="Changes the project; undoable and attributed">mutating</span>

Look at a sequence at any time without playing: renders through the sequence's live camera (cuts and shots) with every keyed property and animation applied, then restores the scene. times=[...] returns up to 8 images (a storyboard). Render a whole shot to disk with fps + from/to + save_dir (PNG frames, e.g. for a video). persist=true instead leaves the editor showing that time (sequencer preview). Only while editing. Example: {"sequence": "Intro", "times": [0, 2.5, 5]}.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence` | any | yes | Entity with a sequencer, or a sequence path played by one |  |
| `time` | number |  | Seconds |  |
| `times` | number[] |  | Several times (max 8 images) |  |
| `fps` | number |  | Render frames at this rate between from and to into save_dir |  |
| `from` | number |  | Render range start (default 0) |  |
| `to` | number |  | Render range end (default: the sequence length) |  |
| `save_dir` | string |  | Project-relative folder for rendered frames (frame_0000.png ...) |  |
| `camera` | string |  | Look through the sequence's camera (default) or the editor camera | `sequence` `editor` |
| `width` | integer |  | Image width (default 768) |  |
| `height` | integer |  | Image height (default 432) |  |
| `persist` | boolean |  | Keep showing this time in the editor (sets sequencer preview/time) |  |
| `include_image` | boolean |  | Return the images (default true; false = just render / save) |  |
| `transient` | boolean |  | Only show `time` in the editor viewport (no capture, not saved) until clear |  |
| `clear` | boolean |  | End a transient scrub |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    sequence_scrub {"sequence": "Intro", "times": [0, 2.5, 5]}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call sequence_scrub '{"sequence": "Intro", "times": [0, 2.5, 5]}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "sequence_scrub",
        "arguments": {
          "sequence": "Intro",
          "times": [
            0,
            2.5,
            5
          ]
        }
      }
    }
    ```
